# `canopymodel`: canopy height surface {#sec-canopymodel}

## What it does

`canopymodel` builds a canopy height model (CHM): a raster in which each
cell holds the height of the highest point in that cell above the ground
surface. A CHM is the starting point for tree detection (`canopymaxima`,
`treeseg`, `pipeline`), for canopy gap mapping, and for any analysis of
canopy surface shape (`gridsurfacestats`).

A cell that no point falls in is left empty (NoData) rather than filled,
so empty cells show exactly where the data has no returns.

## Example commands

The example builds three CHMs from the same points and ground surface:
plain, smoothed, and slope-adjusted.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/canopymodel_commands.md >}}

## Options used

| Option | Value | What it does |
|:--------|:--------------------|:-------------------------|
| `/ground` | `out/ground_dem.tif` | Ground surface subtracted from each point's elevation. Without it, the raster holds raw elevations (a surface model rather than a height model). |
| `/cellsize` | `3` | CHM cell size, 3 ft. |
| `/output` | `out/chm.tif` | The CHM (GeoTIFF). Required. |
| `/smooth` | `3` | Smooth with a 3 x 3 cell moving average. Empty cells stay empty; they are not filled from their neighbours. |
| `/slope` | | Measure each point's height perpendicular to the local slope of the ground surface rather than straight up. The two differ only where the ground is sloped. |
| `/gpu` | | Enable CUDA GPU acceleration for point cloud rasterization and smoothing filter. Automatically falls back to multi-threaded CPU execution if no compatible CUDA GPU is available. |
| `/nogpu` | | Explicitly disable CUDA GPU acceleration and run strictly on the CPU. |

: Options used in the `canopymodel` examples. {#tbl-options-canopymodel}

## GPU Acceleration

When compiled with CUDA support and executed on a system with an NVIDIA GPU, `canopymodel` supports the `/gpu` switch:

1. **Tile-origin normalization**: Point coordinates are normalized relative to $(x_{min}, y_{max})$ on the host using double precision before device upload, preserving millimeter precision in 32-bit GPU registers across large state plane coordinates.
2. **Atomic integer reinterpretation**: Above-ground heights are updated in device memory using hardware-accelerated `atomicMax` on 32-bit reinterpreted float representations.
3. **Device spatial smoothing**: When `/smooth:n` is specified, a 2D separable box convolution executes directly in GPU device memory prior to host download, avoiding intermediate host memory copies.
4. **Resilient fallback**: If CUDA device allocation or initialization fails, the tool logs an informational message and automatically falls back to CPU multi-threaded execution.

## Outputs

One GeoTIFF per run with one band, `canopy_height`, in feet above ground.

## Results

@fig-canopymodel-maps shows the three CHMs on one height scale. All three
show distinct crowns separated by gaps. The smoothed version is softer.
On this gently sloping tile, the slope-adjusted version is nearly
identical to the plain one. Single empty cells (dark grey) inside the
canopy are cells no point fell in; they stay in the same place after
smoothing.

{{< include ../examples/fragments/canopymodel_figures.md >}}

In the side view in @fig-canopymodel-profile, the plain CHM line (blue)
rides along the top of the point cloud, and the smoothed line (orange)
follows it with softened peaks.

## Checks

@tbl-checks-canopymodel confirms that no cell is taller than the tallest
point above ground or more than 1 ft below ground, that the CHM agrees
with a CHM built in R from the same points, that `/smooth:3` reduces
cell-to-cell variation, and that `/slope` changes the surface.
